evals.name: bootstrap
evals.prompt: Set up writing conventions for this project.
evals.expected_output: A Writing Conventions block in CLAUDE.md with the shared core, the mode table, and a reader roster or the insider default; one question about who reads the project's output.
expectations: CLAUDE.md gains a Writing Conventions section marked with a `<!-- managed by /red-pen -->` breadcrumb
The section covers all four output types (spec/plan, code comment, code/diff/commit, chat) with a one-line rule each
The section states the reader default or a reader roster
The agent asks exactly one question about who reads the project's output, or proposes a roster and asks to confirm it
The section is at most 280 words excluding any roster table, and nothing is offloaded to a second file
No project policy is invented that the repository cannot support (no Slack templates, terminology tables, or log formats conjured from a 6-line CLAUDE.md)
The existing Project and Key Files sections of CLAUDE.md survive unchanged
The chat reply is at most 150 words with at most one bold lead

evals.name: fresh-spec
evals.prompt: Write up a plan for adding rate limiting to the API. Product and eng will both read it. Put it in docs/rate_limiting.md.
evals.expected_output: A short plan with a prose preamble naming both readers, decisions in chose/over/because form, no re-raising of the Redis, 429, or per-key decisions already in NOTES.md, asks (per-tenant quotas, mobile limit) in their own section, no Overview/Next steps headers, near the 300-word budget.
expectations: docs/rate_limiting.md is created
The document opens with a prose preamble (no heading) that names product and engineering readers and says how each should read it
The Redis, 429 + Retry-After, and per-API-key decisions from NOTES.md are treated as settled, not re-raised as open choices
Per-tenant quotas and the mobile-app limit each appear as an open item or as an explicit decision with a revisit trigger, never inside the preamble
At least one decision is written in 'chose A over B because C' form with a revisit trigger
Assumptions appear as a tick-list
At least one risk is written as a conditional ('X breaks if Y')
No Overview, Introduction, Background, or Next steps section under any name (a 'Why' section that is background counts)
The whole file is at most 300 words excluding the title, or the document's first line says it exceeded the budget and why
Every rate, limit, duration, and estimate in the document traces to NOTES.md or CLAUDE.md or is labelled as a proposed default (HTTP status codes are exempt)
The chat reply is at most 120 words, names what needs the user's call, and does not enumerate the document's decisions

evals.name: too-long
evals.prompt: I asked which rate limiting algorithm to use and you replied with draft_reply.md. too long, too wordy. try again.
evals.expected_output: A rewritten reply, answer first, a lean, well under 150 words, no explanation of why the first was long, no headers, no performative phrases.
expectations: The new reply is at most 120 words
The first paragraph names the pick
The reasons for the pick, if there are three or more, appear as a list rather than run together in a paragraph
At least one reason ties to the project (the partner burst incident), not a generic trade-off
No headers and no performative phrases
The reply does not explain why the previous reply was long and does not apologize
The reply does not restate decisions NOTES.md already settles (Redis, 429, per-key) as if new
No default numbers are invented without a source or without being labelled as a proposal
The reply does not close with an offer to do more

evals.name: edit-target
evals.prompt: red-pen grid_section.md. The reader is product management.
evals.expected_output: An edited grid_section.md that keeps every rule, capability, and pointer but states the deliberate-replacement fact once or twice instead of ten times, drops 'This is / That is' openers and forward references, and a short report: one line, one before/after paragraph, a table of at most four symptom rows.
expectations: An edited grid_section.md is written and is shorter than the original

All five subsections 6.1-6.5 remain and these rules survive: fill a 90-minute gap with two 45s, align to edges left by existing bookings, closeness-to-noon stays the ranking, the two adaptive-grid shapes, the duration/grid entanglement and its verification need
Sentences asserting that edge-based ranking was deliberately replaced or rejected number at most 3 (original: 10)
Sentences opening with 'This is', 'That is', or 'That's' number at most 2 (original: 9)
The Duration/Grid definition bullets and the three packing-mechanism bullets remain as lists, not collapsed into prose
No content is added that is not in the source section
The chat reply has, in order: one line saying what was written and preserved, one before/after paragraph pair, then a symptom table of at most four rows; nothing else
The chat reply is at most 150 words outside the before/after pair and contains no word count
evals.input_note: grid_section.md is an illustration written in the style of an unedited AI requirements draft, for an advisory firm's booking tool.

evals.name: code-comments
evals.prompt: Add retry with exponential backoff to WebhookClient.send: 3 attempts on 5xx, fail fast on 4xx. Write the commit message too.
evals.expected_output: A small diff to src/webhook_client.py with no comments that restate code or narrate the session, comment density matching the file, no TODO stubs, and a commit message with a verb-led subject under 72 chars and a body only if there is a non-obvious decision.
expectations: send() retries up to 3 attempts on 5xx responses with backoff between attempts and returns without retrying on 4xx
Every comment and docstring in the file describes what the code actually does
No comment or docstring restates what the adjacent code visibly does, and none narrates the session
An edge case that the wording 'fail fast on 4xx' covers but its intent may not (429, or transport errors) is surfaced to the user in the reply or noted in a comment
No TODO or stub placeholders in delivered code
The commit subject is verb-led and under 72 characters
The commit body, if present, carries only non-obvious decisions and does not restate the diff
The diff is confined to webhook_client.py plus tests; NOTES.md, the constructor signature, and retry semantics beyond 5xx are untouched unless the reply surfaces the change as an ask with a reason

evals.name: chat-answer
evals.prompt: Should the admin panel use JWT or session cookies?
evals.expected_output: A reply whose first sentence is the answer with a lean, under 150 words, no headers, no restating the question, no 'Great question'.
expectations: The first sentence is the answer with a lean
The reply is at most 150 words
No headers and at most one bold phrase
The reason given ties to something in the project context, not generic textbook trade-offs only
Technical claims are correct (a wrong statement about SameSite, CSRF, or JWT revocation fails)
The reply notes that the project has no admin panel or auth yet, or asks one question that depends on it
The reply ends with at most one question and no trailing offer

evals.name: stale-draft
evals.expected_output: An edited design.md that drops the Overview/Background/Next steps scaffolding and narration, and that flags rather than silently keeps or silently fixes the two claims contradicting NOTES.md (database choice open; rate limiting approach undecided).
expectations: The edited design.md has no Overview, Background, or Next steps scaffolding headers
Narration sentences (In this document we will cover...) are removed
The claim that the database choice is still open is flagged to the user as contradicting the record, not kept silently and not silently rewritten
The claim that the rate limiting approach is undecided is flagged to the user as contradicting NOTES.md, not kept silently and not silently rewritten
The rewritten rate-limiting text matches NOTES.md's three decisions (Redis state, 429 + Retry-After, per-API-key)
The storage choice, which is genuinely open, remains an ask with a stated lean
No open questions or assumptions are introduced beyond what the draft, NOTES.md, CLAUDE.md, and the project's source files contain
The chat reply has: one line naming what was written and the stale claims found, one before/after pair, a symptom table of at most four rows; nothing else
The chat reply is at most 150 words outside the before/after pair and contains no word count

evals.name: pr-description
evals.prompt: Write the PR description for the webhook-retry branch. changes.md summarizes what changed.
evals.expected_output: A PR description that opens with one sentence saying the return-type change needs judgment and the renames are mechanical, surfaces the return-type change as a deviation from the ask with its reason, and does not list every file.
expectations: The description opens with one or two sentences naming the return-type change as the part needing the reviewer's judgment and the renames as mechanical
The return-type change is surfaced as a deviation from the original ask, with the reason (callers need attempt counts)
No per-file change inventory
The description body is at most 200 words
No markdown headers (terse label lines such as 'Risk:' are allowed)
Every concrete number and claim traces to changes.md or the source file (invented test contents or implementation details not in changes.md fail)
The chat text around the description is at most 60 words
